journey:christ-the-redeemer-rio.a: Heitor da Silva Costa (design and engineering), Paul Landowski (sculptor), Gheorghe Leonida (face)
journey:christ-the-redeemer-rio.c: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (head and hands modelled in Paris)
journey:christ-the-redeemer-rio.l: Corcovado mountain, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
journey:christ-the-redeemer-rio.m: Reinforced concrete clad in a mosaic of soapstone tiles

x.summary: Standing with open arms on the summit of Corcovado, about 700 metres above Rio de Janeiro, Christ the Redeemer has become one of the most recognised images of Christ in the world. Its simple, streamlined Art Deco form makes it readable from the city far below, and the outstretched arms form both a cross and a gesture of embrace. It was dedicated on 12 October 1931 and has become a symbol of Brazil itself.
facts: The statue is about 30 metres tall on an 8-metre pedestal, and its arms span roughly 28 metres.
Its reinforced-concrete frame is covered with a mosaic of thousands of small triangular soapstone tiles, a stone chosen for its durability and ease of working.
It was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007, and it is regularly struck by lightning: a 2014 strike dislodged a finger on the right hand.
